paper.title: ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities
paper.central_claim: ChatGPT can solve diverse robotics tasks zero-shot across form factors through prompt engineering and a high-level function library, with a user on the loop and conversational closed-loop reasoning.

signatures.object: Drone, manipulator and navigation controllers generated from natural language
signatures.information: Human-authored API signatures, descriptions, environment/task constraints and sometimes predefined object positions or text observations; model has no automatic raw sensor access by default
signatures.operation: Implement backend high-level function library; prompt allowed calls and output format; generate Python/control logic; human analyzes or simulates and returns feedback; approve and deploy code
signatures.output: User-approved robot program; conversational commands in selected examples
signatures.conditions: Correct API wrappers and environment descriptions; knowledgeable/safety-conscious user and usable simulator
signatures.feedback: Human critique or simulator observations; some text perception-action dialogue; mostly no post-code model feedback
signatures.selection_rule: Human approves quality/safety, otherwise supplies corrections; no standardized measured acceptance rule
signatures.data: Illustrative hand-designed task prompts and selected conversation excerpts
signatures.persistence: Current dialog and approved task code; no cross-task accepted harness optimization or learned policy updates
signatures.later_use: Run approved program on chosen robot/simulator; code reuse only ordinary engineering
signatures.claimed_effect: Accessible platform-independent task solving and conversational correction
signatures.failure_boundary: Hallucinated calls, wrong frames/assumptions, human dependence; full final code/correction logs not fixed

gap.author_gap: Existing robot language interfaces have restricted scope or open-loop use; nontechnical users need natural dialog that produces deployable robot behavior.
gap.checked_gap: A useful interface-design question: domain wrappers and explicit permitted calls can constrain generated control code. Supplied examples show API-specification and feedback sensitivity, but do not establish general reliability or measured improvement over the nearest code-generation systems.
